sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (submitted by Editor, Ethnologue, SIL International). 2019. Change Request Number 2019-032: Retire [tbb] Tapeba (adopted 2020-01-23). 5 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; it is a code-retirement record. Rationale (p. 2): 'Ethnologue (1996) declared that the Tapeba ethnic group, numbering 984, was monolingual in Portuguese [por]. Hammarstrom (2015) says that Tapeba is unattested and cannot be asserted to have been a separate language.. There was never a language called Tapeba, only a Portuguese-speaking group representing various languages, now all extinct.' Reason ticked: 'There is no evidence that the language exists.'

sources.citation: Fabre, Alain. 2005- [entry last modified 2009-10-09]. Diccionario etnolingüístico y guía bibliográfica de los pueblos indígenas sudamericanos: TAPEBA. Electronic edition, 1 p.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States (p. 1): 'Lengua no clasificada o inclasificable por falta de datos. No figura en Loukotka (1968) ni tampoco en Tovar & Larrucea de Tovar (1984).' and 'Nadie parece hablar su idioma ancestral y todos son actualmente hablantes de portugués (Ethnologue 1996).' Bibliography is entirely ethnographic (Barretto Filho 1989-2000, CEDI 1991, Gomes 1985, Hjerpe 1998, Nobre 2000, Oliveira 1999); no wordlist or grammar cited.

sources.citation: Barretto Filho, Henyo Trindade. 1998 [rev. 2021-01-25]. Tapeba. In: Povos Indígenas no Brasil, Instituto Socioambiental (online encyclopedia entry).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or on any Tapeba language; ethnographic/historical entry (ethnogenesis from Potiguara, Cariri, Tremembé remnants; Tupi etymology of the toponym 'tapeba' < itapeva). No linguistic data.
